title: OTWD moderation decision
description: The recorded outcome for a submission, with who or what decided and why. Decisions are appended to the submission log and never edited. An appeal produces a new decision that refers to the earlier one.

outcome.description: approved: applied as submitted. edited_and_approved: applied after a moderator corrected it (amendments lists the corrections). rejected: not applied. needs_info: waiting for the contributor to answer the public note.

routing.description: How routing sent the submission to whoever decided it, with what routing read from the submission: its kind, its record type and the fields it touches. The fixed checks derive whether the submission is on the always-human list from these, using the creation kinds, closures, merges and the safety fact markers (x-otwd-safety-fact) in the record type's schema, so a routing rule cannot approve one by declaring always_human false.

route.description: human_review: a moderator's queue. auto_approval: approved by a routing rule, never used for the always-human list (new records of every record type, closures, merges, safety facts).

submission_kind.description: The kind of the submission decided.

record_type.description: The record type the submission creates or changes.

fields.description: For update_facts: every fact and facility the submission sets or removes.

always_human.description: True when the submission is on the always-human list. The fixed checks derive it, and it must be true whenever the kind or a field puts the submission on the list.

verdict_ids.description: The verdicts available when the decision was made. A verdict informs a decision and is never one.

code.description: For example confirmed_by_seed_source, duplicate_of_existing_site or copied_text.

public_note.description: The message shown to the contributor and returned to the partner app. Required for rejected and needs_info.

amendments.description: For edited_and_approved: each amendment the moderator made before approving, with the submitted and the applied value.

applied.description: The value as applied, or null when the moderator dropped the field.

merge.description: For an approved request_merge: the surviving record and the records that now redirect to it, all of one record type.

change_seqs.description: For approved and edited_and_approved: the changes the decision produced. A merge produces one change per record involved.

appeal_of.description: When this decision answers an appeal: the decision appealed against.

allOf.description: A routing rule may only approve, only on the auto_approval route, and only a submission outside the always-human list. The fixed checks derive membership of the list from routing's submission_kind, record_type and fields, so the always_human false required here is a cross-check, never the rule itself.

Decider.description: Who or what made the decision. moderator: a person. routing_rule: an automatic approval rule in the fixed routing code, allowed only outside the always-human list. The AI never decides.

moderator_id.description: Moderators are contributors with moderation rights, so they use contributor IDs.
